target_customer: Scientists, research labs, journals, societies and publishers who need interactive, reusable scientific publishing
problem: Scientific reports are static documents detached from data and code; Curvenote builds modular, versioned content blocks and publishing tools so figures and data stay live and reusable.
business_model: Open-core SaaS with enterprise features (scientific content management system and journal publishing)

founders.name: Steve Purves
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 20 years building software for scientists and engineers, R&D work for oil and gas majors, founding member of an open geoscience society.

competitors.name: Authorea
competitors.traction_then: Used by researchers, listed in writing-tool roundups

competitors.name: Overleaf
competitors.what: Collaborative LaTeX editor; CERN adopted it as preferred platform in 2017

competitors.name: Manubot
competitors.what: Open-source system for collaborative manuscript writing on GitHub
competitors.traction_then: Featured in a 2020 Nature technology feature

technical_complexity.rationale: Block-based versioned content model with Jupyter integration and a web editor; standard engineering with hard data-model design for a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Open-core with open formats (MyST Markdown) lowers lock-in; value depends on adoption by journals and societies.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying the block model; the company reports journal and society customers through 2025 and 2026.

market_need_then: Open science and reproducibility pressure in 2020 and 2021, plus the move of research toward notebooks and live data; the YC application framed static PDFs as the pain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led and open science oriented; tagline Build connected knowledge

branding.brand_signature: Curvenote is a registered trademark with the tagline Build connected knowledge
branding.community_and_virality: Contributes to MyST Markdown and open science communities and writes on a Medium blog; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within open science circles and used for conference proceedings, but little brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Curvenote has stayed small and active, building open-core publishing tools for scientists, with journal and society deployments in 2024 to 2026. Funding is thin in the public record, so its stalled or growing status is unclear. The founders' scientific software background fits the niche, and there is no evidence of an exit, shutdown or large round.
notes: A social media repost around July 2025 pointed to a headline about a 1.4 million USD seed round; no outlet or investor list was opened, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Funding searches mostly returned unrelated companies with similar names (Curvestone AI). Overleaf and Authorea were listed in a 2020 Nature feature; the Overleaf CERN 2017 date came from a separate university guide snippet.
